name: Hypatia
summary: Hypatia was a Neoplatonist philosopher, astronomer, and mathematician who lived in Alexandria, at that time in the province of Egypt and a major city of the Roman Empire.

facts.text: Hypatia was a Neoplatonist philosopher, astronomer, and mathematician who lived in Alexandria, at that time in the province of Egypt and a major city of the Roman Empire.
facts.context: Hypatia's background gives readers a concrete entry point into Science, Math & Technology.

facts.text: In Alexandria, Hypatia was a prominent thinker who taught subjects including philosophy and astronomy, and in her lifetime was renowned as a great teacher and a wise counselor.
facts.context: Hypatia's challenge makes the card about pressure and choice, not just fame.

facts.text: Not the only fourth century Alexandrian female mathematician, Hypatia was preceded by Pandrosion.
facts.context: Hypatia's turning point shows how one moment can redirect a public life.

facts.text: However, Hypatia is the first female mathematician whose life is reasonably well recorded.
facts.context: Hypatia's contribution helps explain why this profile belongs in the People Library.

facts.text: Hypatia wrote a commentary on Diophantus's thirteen-volume Arithmetica, which may survive in part, having been interpolated into Diophantus's original text, and another commentary on Apollonius of Perga's treatise on conic sections, which has not survived.
facts.context: Hypatia's influence connects one short Fact to a wider historical ripple.
